- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.20), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–4 days after spike.  
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days are above true outcome, apply mean reversion: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); cap forecast at 10–15% above recent 7-day average to avoid overreach.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
